symptoms: Device shows connected to Wi-Fi but websites do not load; internet access unavailable.
possible_causes: Router or ISP outage; incorrect IP or DNS settings; captive portal; device network adapter issue.
diagnostic_checks: Check whether other devices can access the internet; confirm airplane mode is off; disconnect and reconnect to Wi-Fi; check IP configuration; test access to a known website.
resolution_steps: Reconnect to the correct Wi-Fi network; complete any sign-in portal; restart the device; renew the IP address or flush DNS only if permitted by company policy; contact the network team if multiple devices are affected.
escalation_condition: Multiple users or devices are affected, or connectivity remains unavailable after basic checks.

issue: Outlook does not open or keeps crashing
symptoms: Outlook closes unexpectedly, freezes during startup, or does not open.
possible_causes: Corrupted Outlook profile; faulty add-in; outdated application; damaged Office installation; mailbox or service issue.
diagnostic_checks: Check whether Outlook on the web works; restart Outlook and the computer; note any error message; check Microsoft 365 service status if available; try safe mode only if authorized.
resolution_steps: Install approved Office updates; disable a recently added problematic add-in if permitted; create or repair the Outlook profile following IT procedures; use Outlook on the web as a temporary workaround.
escalation_condition: Outlook on the web also fails, several users are affected, or profile repair does not resolve the issue.

issue: User cannot sign in or account is locked
symptoms: Sign-in fails, account is locked, or the user receives an authentication error.
possible_causes: Incorrect username or password; account lockout; expired password; MFA issue; account disabled.
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the correct username and sign-in page; capture the exact error; check keyboard Caps Lock and input language; verify whether MFA is working; check account status using approved tools.
resolution_steps: Use the organization's approved password-reset or account-unlock process; complete MFA verification; do not ask the user to share their password; confirm access after the reset.
escalation_condition: Account is disabled, MFA cannot be recovered, or approved self-service reset fails.

symptoms: Print job remains queued, printer is offline, or no page is printed.
possible_causes: Printer disconnected; paper jam; low toner; incorrect default printer; stuck print queue; driver issue.
diagnostic_checks: Check power, cables and network connection; inspect paper and toner; confirm the correct printer is selected; check printer status and queue; test with another user or device if possible.
resolution_steps: Clear the print queue if authorized; remove paper jams safely; reload paper; set the correct printer as default; restart the printer; reinstall or update the approved driver if required.
escalation_condition: Hardware fault is indicated, printer is shared and affects multiple users, or approved driver troubleshooting fails.

symptoms: Applications take a long time to open; system freezes or responds slowly.
possible_causes: Too many startup applications; low disk space; high CPU or memory usage; pending updates; malware or hardware issue.
diagnostic_checks: Ask when the slowdown started; check Task Manager for unusually high CPU, memory or disk usage; check available disk space; note whether one application or the whole device is affected; check for pending approved updates.
resolution_steps: Close unnecessary applications; restart the computer; free disk space using approved cleanup methods; install approved updates; raise a security ticket if malware is suspected. Do not disable security software.
escalation_condition: Repeated freezes, suspected malware, hardware warnings, or performance remains poor after basic checks.

symptoms: VPN client shows connection failed, authentication failed, or remains stuck connecting.
possible_causes: Internet connection problem; expired credentials; MFA failure; VPN service outage; outdated VPN client; device compliance issue.
diagnostic_checks: Confirm normal internet access first; capture the VPN error and time; verify username and MFA; check whether colleagues are affected; confirm the approved VPN client is being used.
resolution_steps: Reconnect to the internet; retry the approved sign-in process; restart the VPN client; install approved client updates; follow the organization's device-compliance and MFA procedure.
escalation_condition: VPN service appears unavailable, access policy blocks the user, or connection fails after approved checks.

symptoms: A business application freezes, displays a not-responding message, or stops responding to input.
possible_causes: Application defect; insufficient system resources; network or backend dependency issue; corrupted local cache; recent update.
diagnostic_checks: Record application name and version; capture exact error and time; check whether other applications work; determine whether other users are affected; check approved application status or logs if access is available.
resolution_steps: Wait briefly if the application is processing; save work if possible; close and reopen the application; restart the device if appropriate; retry after checking service status. Do not delete application data unless instructed.
escalation_condition: Issue affects multiple users, repeats after restart, or application logs indicate a backend or product defect.

issue: No network connection on a wired desktop
symptoms: Desktop shows no Ethernet connection or cannot reach internal or external network resources.
possible_causes: Loose or damaged cable; inactive switch port; network adapter disabled; DHCP issue; network outage.
diagnostic_checks: Check Ethernet cable at both ends; inspect link lights; confirm adapter is enabled; test another known-good cable if permitted; check whether nearby users are affected; record any IP configuration error.
resolution_steps: Reconnect the cable; use an approved working port or cable if available; enable the network adapter if it was disabled; restart the device; escalate suspected port or DHCP issues.
escalation_condition: No link light, multiple users are affected, or network configuration/port changes are required.

issue: Windows blue screen or unexpected restart
symptoms: Windows displays a blue screen, restarts unexpectedly, or repeatedly fails to boot.
possible_causes: Driver issue; failed update; hardware fault; overheating; system file corruption.
diagnostic_checks: Record the stop code and time; ask whether new hardware, drivers or updates were installed; check whether the device can start normally; note frequency and any recent changes.
resolution_steps: Follow the organization's approved recovery procedure; disconnect newly attached peripherals if safe; use approved recovery or driver rollback steps only with authorization; preserve error details for investigation.
escalation_condition: Repeated blue screens, boot failure, suspected hardware fault, or recovery steps require administrator access.

symptoms: A payment API request returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error; payment operation may fail or have an unknown outcome.
possible_causes: Unhandled application exception; backend dependency failure; database issue; deployment regression; resource exhaustion.
diagnostic_checks: Record timestamp, endpoint, request or correlation ID and environment; inspect application logs and stack traces; check API health and dependency status; compare error rate with recent deployments; verify whether the payment was actually processed before retrying.
resolution_steps: Follow the incident runbook; alert the backend/application team; preserve logs and correlation IDs; check dependency health; avoid repeated payment retries until transaction status and idempotency are confirmed. Do not expose secrets or payment data in logs.
escalation_team: Backend / Application Engineering and Payments Operations
escalation_condition: Any production payment failure, repeated HTTP 500 responses, possible duplicate/uncertain transaction, or suspected data integrity issue.

issue: Password reset email or MFA code not received
symptoms: User requests a password reset or MFA code but does not receive the expected message.
possible_causes: Incorrect registered contact; email filtering or delay; authenticator device unavailable; notification service issue; account contact details outdated.
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the registered recovery method without asking for passwords or codes; check spam/junk folder; verify device time and network; check whether other notifications arrive; capture the time of the request.
resolution_steps: Use only the approved alternate verification and recovery process; check spam/junk; retry once after a short wait; update recovery details through the authorized identity process.
escalation_condition: Recovery method is inaccessible, registered details are incorrect, or verification cannot be completed.

issue: Shared folder or network drive access denied
symptoms: User cannot open a shared folder or mapped network drive and receives access denied or path unavailable.
possible_causes: Missing permissions; incorrect path; VPN/network unavailable; account group membership change; file server outage.
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the exact shared path; check network or VPN connectivity; ask whether the issue affects one folder or several; compare access with an authorized colleague; capture the exact error.
resolution_steps: Reconnect to the approved network or VPN; verify the path; submit an access request through the approved process; do not change permissions or use another person's credentials.
escalation_condition: Permission changes are needed, multiple users are affected, or the file server is unavailable.
